one_sentence_fix: Spend the next round making the three declared devices actually render: slide 03's dimension call with real extension lines and arrowheads, slide 05's emissive grille as the light source the dossier says it is, and slide 09's five-sheet trail with the solid-versus-phantom outlines visible at feed scale.
weakest_in_plain_language: The artwork does not do what the storyboard says it does. This is one of the best-planned decks the studio has produced: the empty DUE field in the same corner on all nine slides while the counter beside it advances, the read-versus-403-versus-unpublished paper grammar, the decision to render every document blank because the page never prints type it could not read. On the page most of that argument is missing. The carpet weave the prototype called the difference between a failing composition score and a passing one is invisible on every slide. The paper sheets that carry the whole motif are flat grey polygons with no shadow. Slide 03's fully drawn dimension with no number, which the dossier calls the slide's whole argument, has no extension lines and no arrowheads. Slide 05's grille, declared the deck's brightest light, renders as a dark unlit speaker. Slide 09's five-asked-one-answered payoff shows two or three sheets and no visible difference between a solid outline and a phantom one. The toy is beautiful and the writing is rigorous, and between them sits a set of promises the render never kept. That is what one pixel-critic round instead of four costs, and it is exactly what the second and third rounds are for.
